project.setup.description: Get an existing project's Windows SDK and Windows App SDK dependencies in place: restore pinned packages after cloning, generate C++/WinRT headers, or add Windows platform support to a project that is not WinUI.

toolchain.prereqs.description: Install or repair developer machine prerequisites (SDKs, command-line tools, Developer Mode) and verify their versions.

winui.build.description: Build, run, and debug a WinUI 3 app: build errors, startup crashes, and Native AOT publish.

msix.package.description: Turn a desktop app's build output into an MSIX installer, locally or in a build script or CI pipeline.

winui.package.description: Package, sign, and release a WinUI 3 app specifically, including Native AOT and handing the package to the Microsoft Store.

msix.sign.description: Code-sign apps and installers: create test certificates, sign with a PFX or a cloud signing service, and make a certificate trusted on a test machine.

msix.manifest.description: Edit the package manifest: declared capabilities, icons and tile images, command-line aliases, file type associations, URL protocol handlers, and other extensions.

identity.description: Give a desktop app that is not installed as a package a package identity (while debugging, or next to an existing installer) so identity-gated Windows features work.

framework.guidance.description: Framework-specific advice for Windows platform work from Electron, WPF, WinForms, C++, Rust, Flutter, or Tauri.

maui.package.description: Package and sign the Windows target of a .NET MAUI app, including MAUI-specific manifest and publish problems.

api.lookup.description: Check the exact Windows or WinRT types, members, and enum values available in the SDK version a project references.

ui.samples.description: Find a working sample of a WinUI control for a UI need.

winui.design.description: Design or fix WinUI 3 XAML UI: layout, control choice, Fluent look, theming, accessibility, and binding.

winui.review.description: Review WinUI 3 code for bugs and quality problems before it is merged.

winui.migrate.description: Port a WPF app to WinUI 3.

ui.automate.description: Inspect or operate a running desktop app's UI: find elements, click, type, read text, and take screenshots.

ui.test.description: Write and run repeatable automated UI tests for a desktop app.

sandbox.run.description: Run an app in a clean, disposable Windows Sandbox to test it away from the developer's machine.

troubleshoot.description: Diagnose packaging, signing, install, package identity, or SDK setup failures from error codes and logs.

store.publish.description: Submit an app to the Microsoft Store through Partner Center, by hand or from CI.

session.report.description: Analyze a previous AI agent session and report what went wrong. Only when the user explicitly asks.
